meta.audience: The multitude, and the judges among them
principles: An accusation raised by the accused

world_behind.title: The judges are members of the band
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says the men calling for Nephi's arrest belonged to the secret band of Gadianton, which he had just named from the tower.

world_behind.title: They cannot arrest him themselves
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says they feared the people, so they work by stirring the crowd instead.

world_behind.title: Their argument is national strength
world_behind.text: Verse 6 answers the prophecy with power and great cities, and concludes that no enemy can prevail.

world_behind.title: Part of the crowd defends him
world_behind.text: Verses 7 through 9 have people arguing that he is a good man, that he has been right about their sins, and that only a prophet could know the rest.

world_behind.title: Nephi answers with a list of witnesses
world_behind.text: Verses 11 through 22 name Moses, Abraham, men before Abraham, Zenos, Zenock, Ezias, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lehi, and Nephi.

world_behind.title: Ezias appears once in all scripture
world_behind.text: Verse 20 is the only place the name occurs, in a list of prophets who testified of Christ.

world_behind.title: He ends with a checkable sign
world_behind.text: Verses 27 and 28 send them to the judgment-seat to find the chief judge murdered by his brother, both members of the band.

words.text: Treated at Alma 8:13, of the people of Ammonihah. The record uses the word twenty-five times. The judges apply it to speech about the law and about themselves.
The state of being corrupt. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, of the law itself. Mormon adds that Nephi said much that cannot be written, and nothing contrary to God's commandments.
Made of brass. The word occurs once in the record. The King James Bible spells it "brasen" twenty-nine times, and Numbers 21:9 calls the object a serpent of brass.

Broken and humbled in spirit. The record uses the word nine times and the King James Bible five, including the contrite heart of Psalm 51. Verse 15 makes it a condition of the looking that gives life.
A prophet named nowhere else in scripture. The record gives him no words and no story, only a place in a list between Zenock and Isaiah.
Sexual sin outside marriage. The record uses the word three times and the King James Bible thirty-six. Verse 26 pairs it with murders as what they are ripening by.

phrases.term: Why do ye not seize upon this man and bring him forth
phrases.text: The judges ask the crowd to make the arrest. The question is addressed to the people because the judges will not act in their own persons.

phrases.term: Nephi had spoken unto them concerning the corruptness of their law
phrases.text: Mormon's summary of what provoked them. Verse 3 adds that much of what Nephi said cannot be written.

phrases.term: They durst not lay their own hands upon him, for they feared the people
phrases.text: The reason he is still standing. The band controls the courts and is still constrained by public opinion.

phrases.term: We are powerful, and our cities great, therefore our enemies can have no power over us
phrases.text: The counterargument in one sentence. It answers a moral warning with a military inventory.

phrases.term: Let this man alone, for he is a good man
phrases.text: The defense from within the crowd. Verse 8 builds on it: he has been right about their sins, so he is likely right about the rest.

phrases.term: If he had not been a prophet he could not have testified concerning those things
phrases.text: The people's own reasoning, reported as theirs. The record lets a crowd make the argument instead of the prophet.

phrases.term: Have ye not read that God gave power unto one man, even Moses
phrases.text: Nephi's first witness and his first argument. If God gave power to one man then, the dispute about power given now has an answer.

phrases.term: As he lifted up the brazen serpent in the wilderness, even so shall he be lifted up
phrases.text: Moses read as testimony of Christ. Verse 15 adds the condition: look with faith and a contrite spirit, and live.

phrases.term: Zenock, and also Ezias, and also Isaiah, and Jeremiah
phrases.text: Four names in a row, two of them outside the Bible. Nephi treats the plates of brass and the prophets of Judah as one continuous record.

phrases.term: Do ye not behold that the seed of Zedekiah are with us
phrases.text: The argument turns to something in the room. The people of Zarahemla are offered as living evidence that Jerusalem fell as Jeremiah said.

phrases.term: Your judge is murdered, and he lieth in his blood
phrases.text: The sign that closes the sermon. It can be verified by walking to the judgment-seat, and Helaman 9 opens with five men running there.

verses.label: v. 1–6
verses.title: The judges move
verses.text: Judges belonging to the band cry out for Nephi to be seized and condemned, asking why the people let him revile against them and the law. He had spoken of the corruptness of their law, and much he said was not written, and nothing was contrary to God's commandments. They are angry at his plainness about their secret works, but dare not touch him for fear of the people, so they tell the crowd he condemns them and their cities, and answer that their power and great cities make it impossible.

verses.label: v. 7–10
verses.title: The crowd divides
verses.text: Some cry out to leave him alone, calling him a good man whose words will come true without repentance, noting that he has testified rightly about their iniquities and must therefore know what is coming, and that only a prophet could. Fear keeps his opponents off him, and seeing that he has favor with some, Nephi speaks again.

verses.label: v. 11–15
verses.title: Moses
verses.text: He asks whether they have not read that God gave one man power to part the Red Sea for their fathers and close it on the Egyptians. If God gave that man power, the dispute about his own is answered. He adds that denying him denies the fathers and Moses, who testified of the Messiah, lifting the brazen serpent as a figure of one lifted up, so that whoever looks with faith and a contrite spirit lives.

verses.label: v. 16–20
verses.title: The chain of prophets
verses.text: All the holy prophets from Moses back to Abraham testified of these things. Abraham saw his coming and rejoiced, and men before Abraham were called after the order of the Son, so that redemption was shown thousands of years ahead. Since Abraham many have testified: Zenos, who was slain for it, and Zenock, Ezias, Isaiah, and Jeremiah, whose word about Jerusalem is known to have come true.

verses.label: v. 21–23
verses.title: Evidence in the room
verses.text: He asks whether they will dispute that Jerusalem fell, or that Zedekiah's sons were killed except Mulek, whose seed is among them, driven out of Jerusalem. Lehi was driven out for testifying, and Nephi and nearly all the fathers testified of Christ and rejoiced in his day, and he manifested himself to them.

verses.label: v. 24–26
verses.title: The charge
verses.text: Knowing these things and unable to deny them without lying, they have sinned by rejecting them despite every evidence in heaven and earth. Instead of laying up treasures in heaven where nothing corrupts, they are heaping up wrath for the day of judgment, and are ripening for destruction.

verses.label: v. 27–28
verses.title: The sign
verses.text: It is at their doors. He tells them to go to the judgment-seat and look: the judge is murdered and lies in his blood, killed by his brother who wants the seat, and both belong to the band whose author is Gadianton and the evil one.

chapter.title: The accusers are the accused
chapter.text: Verse 1 identifies the judges demanding an arrest as members of the band Nephi had just described. The charge and the crime are the same men.

chapter.title: Power is used indirectly
chapter.text: They control the courts and still work through the crowd, because verse 4 says they fear the people. Authority that cannot be used openly is doing something else.

chapter.title: The people make the argument for him
chapter.text: Verses 7 through 9 have ordinary listeners reasoning from his accuracy about their sins to his reliability about the future.

chapter.title: The defense is a list of witnesses
chapter.text: Nephi answers a question about his own authority by naming ten others. The claim is placed inside a tradition rather than resting on him.

chapter.title: Two prophets are known only from this record
chapter.text: Ezias appears once in all scripture, and Zenos is reported slain only here. The plates of brass held more than the Bible kept.

chapter.title: Fulfilled prophecy is used as the argument
chapter.text: Verse 20 reasons from Jeremiah's word about Jerusalem, which they know came true, to the coming of the Son of God.

chapter.title: The Mulekites are exhibit one
chapter.text: Verse 21 points at people standing in the land as proof that Jerusalem fell. The audience is itself the evidence.

chapter.title: The sermon ends on something falsifiable
chapter.text: Verse 27 sends them to a specific room to see a specific thing. The prophet stakes the whole address on what they will find there.

applications.title: Notice who wants the crowd to act for them
applications.text: The judges had every power except the willingness to be seen using it. Someone urging you to do what they could do themselves is telling you something.

applications.title: Beware of answering a moral case with an inventory
applications.text: Great cities and power were the whole reply. Strength is not an argument against a warning about conduct.

applications.title: Reason from what someone got right
applications.text: The crowd trusted Nephi about the future because he had been accurate about the present. Track records are usable evidence.

applications.title: Put your claim in a line of witnesses
applications.text: Nephi named ten others rather than standing alone. Showing that you are saying what others have said is stronger than insisting on yourself.

questions.text: What plain thing about my situation would I rather not have said out loud?
What am I refraining from doing only because of who is watching?
What strength am I using as an answer to a warning?
Whose track record have I ignored?
What am I unwilling to look at, though looking would help?
What do I know and cannot deny except by lying?
What am I heaping up instead of laying up?
